segments.text: A massive flash protest outside the seven Lok Kalyan Marg of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, his residence by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and the top leadership of the Congress Party.
Joining me on this special broadcast, Dr. Shama Mohammed, National Spokesperson of the Congress, Dr. Ajay Alok.
National spokesperson of the BJP, Aarti Jairat, is a senior journalist.
She's covered many protests, I'm sure.
Unlike one that's just happened outside Lok Kalyan Mark, Dr. Vikram Singh, former DGP and a security affairs analyst, joins us on the show.
Dr. Shama Mohammed, this is the monsoon session of parliament.
Any discussion should happen on the floor of the house.
Top leaders, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, all on the streets, explain this, ma'am.
You know, Gaurav, two things.
Before 2014, today's topic would have been, you know what, police brutality against our children.
That would have been your topic of discussion.
But after 2014,
The topic changes.
You can't question the government or the police.
Unfair criticism, we question the government.
We question everything that is wrong with the system.
As you watch India Today, you see that, Dr. Shama Mohamad.
But you should act with the topic today this, because the police brutality on our children much more.
And number two, number two, today, Rahul Gandhi... You know, permit me to say, permit me to decide what would be the topic.
Today, Rahul Gandhi is sitting on a dharna outside the Prime Minister's house.
That is my debate, Dr. Shama Mohamad.
Yeah, so I'm going to say, wait.
Now, you have asked what is happening.
Now, when Rahul Gandhi is not on the street, that is what my leader is.
He is saying that I'm out there with the students, saying this is wrong, what is happening.
First, peaceful protest should be allowed in this country.
During our time, you remember, Nirbhaya,
We allowed the peaceful protests to happen.
They were in Delhi, South Delhi.
Everybody knows where it was in the Ram Leela Maidan.
We never stopped.
And that is what democracy is all about.
And all over the world, people protest when there are problems.
Now, these are young students protesting, some of them with their parents.
What we saw yesterday, a 12-year-old girl beaten up.
Another child is in the ICU.
You know, I have a 19-year-old son.
Another, you know, another one, a stick, a police was putting a stick up from behind her.
I mean, police brutalities, the way they were beating them up, as if they were some thugs, these kids.
Of course, they are upset when there is an issue like this.
And let's understand the last leak in NEET happened at the NTN, National Testing Agency.
That is the most important part of this government, where the exams are set.
Now, who is responsible?
In a democracy, the most important thing is accountability.

Nobody resigns who is accountable, unless you see Keith Stammer has resigned as the prime minister of UK, because he was responsible for many things that happened, including the ambassador who he sent to the United States in the Epstein fires.
Look at the way that is how everybody is accountable.
Here, Dharmendra Prasan refuses to resign.
The prime minister refuses to ask him to resign.
Nobody from the NTA goes.
So what is happening in this country?
These children, you need to answer to them.
And that is why my leader Rahul Gandhi is out there on the streets saying that if you don't listen to them, then I'm out there going to be with them.
Arrest me.
Put me behind bars.
I will not bow down.
Dr Ajay Alok respond, a discussion that should have happened on the floor of the house in the monsoon session.
Parliament not functioning.
That is why protests are happening on the street.
And the big point, Congress party says government does not even permit protests.
Gaurav, right now on your debate, we are talking of democracy and peaceful protest is a right.
Of course, it's a right.
But in a democracy, even if your title of the debate has to be decided by the political parties, then there is no democracy.
First of all, the very snatching of democracy begins from here, right from the beginning.
Those who have imposed emergency, they are pleading democracy.
This is not democracy.
What Rahul Gandhi has done today is vandalism.
It's an act of anarchy.
It's a lawlessness.
It's absolute frustration.
It's just a knee-jerk reaction what he has done today.
There have been so many instances.
We have been in opposition for so long.
But there's a decorum of the country.
There's a perception of the country.
There's a perception of the opposition.
You are not discussing it in the parliament for the last two days.
You are disrupting the parliament.
We are saying everything will be discussed.
Please go according to the rules and laws.
You are not failing to count that.
You are just raising slogans, putting play cards in the house, both the houses.
You are not letting the house function.
What happens today?
They all gathered today at Rajadjee to greet Khadgeji on his birthday, and then suddenly marched towards the prime minister's house.
This is the way leader of opposition behaves.
This is the fence of responsibility of 56 years old.
What kind of security concerns are there?
Even for himself, forget about the prime minister.
What messages and what images it has thrown in the world?
That's a very pertinent point you raise.
The need has been deconducted.
The students have been inducted.
The results are already out.
I mean, what happens to those students today in Kerala, where water trails and water canyons are used against the students?
Okay, so pertinent points have been raised by both sides.
Before I get Dr. Shamha Mohammed to respond to the points you've raised, Aarti Jairat, a democratic protest, a flash protest outside the Prime Minister's residence, or is this anarchy?
How do you watch Rahul Gandhi's protest or the Congress party's protest outside 7 Lok Kalyan Marg?
Gaurav, you did say that I have been around for a long time.
And so I have seen many, many such protests.
In a democracy, protests happen.
This is not anarchy.
And I think that to describe it as anarchy is a wrong characterization of what democracy is all about.
Democracy is all about dissent.
It's all about the freedom to speak.
And, you know, as long as they weren't vandalizing property or beating up people or, you know, engaging in violence, why not protest?
But, yes, I do agree that Parliament is in session and, you know, issues should be discussed on the floor of the House.
But for that, you need the cooperation of the government as well, not just the opposition, but the government.
And given the fact that the monsoon session started with the protest on the roads, I would have thought that that would be the first topic of discussion in parliament.
But why are our kids out on the roads protesting?
Why?

And I think that this deserves an answer from those who are in charge, which is the government of the day, that what has made, you know, Gaurav, there were eight-year-old kids, ten-year-old kids out on the streets.
You know, in the evening, we saw the streets were littered with chapels and shoes and, you know, juttis and things like that.
Why?
Because all those kids have been beaten up and dragged away by the police.
I mean, come on.
Yeah, but why were eight and ten-year-old kids at the protest in the first place when you talk about a safe environment for children?
Why should children be there in the first place is perhaps a point that may be raised.
Point one, but point two, let me also bring in Dr. Vikram Singh for his opening comments.
Dr. Vikram Singh, as someone who looks at security in India's environment and in the neighborhood very closely,
a flash protest by the opposition outside the prime minister's residence.
BJP spokesperson says that's anarchy.
Congress says it's a right to protest.
How do you look at it?
Right to protest or designated spots to protest not outside the prime minister's residence.
Good evening, Gauravji, and good evening, my esteemed panellists.
I would say that yes, the right to protest peacefully is a fundamental right, a fundamental right.
But with reasonable restrictions, please take adequate precautions and take permission of YD-163 section of the Bharatiya Nagariks Raksha Sanghita, former 144 CRPC.
And the PM's house and the PM's residence is just not a picnic spot.
You have to take pains to take prior permission, give the police to have proper bundle bus.
It cannot be a free-for-all.
And if there is a free-for-all, I would say if the antecedents there, and I would say to one learned panelist, that why were the kids there?
Why were the families there?
You know, Mr. Junaid there is feeding 2,000 people every day at the cost of 8 lakhs to the tune of 2 crore 40 lakhs a month.
There is much more to it than what's in the eye.
And I shudder to think what happened in the parliament yesterday if that could have been replicated at the PM's house.
It cannot.
It's not a laughing matter.
It is not something to be argued upon.
We can certainly debate.
But as a professional police or former police officer and a security person who is in my security, I would say it is the job of the police to ensure foolproof and failproof security of the VVIP.
You cannot take chances and liberties.
And then one call of wisdom from one Neta.
And I'll stop at that.
OK, and I'll get the Congress to respond to what you've said.
But before that, Dr. Ajay Alok, you must respond to what Aarti Jair had said.
In a democracy, opposition has the right to protest.
They should have done it on the floor of the House.
And it's the responsibility of the government to ensure that the House functions.
Take the opposition along.
You had Shashi Tharoor, Congress MP, saying yesterday, if the government does not permit the opposition to ventilate on the floor of the House, protests will happen on the street.
In a parliamentary democracy,
The opposition has its say.
The government, because it has the numbers, will have its way.
At least let the opposition have their say, sir.
Gaurav, I don't say that you don't have a right to protest.
You can protest.
But ma'am said that there was no vandalism.
What happened yesterday?
118 Delhi police officers are injured.
That's not vandalism.
Many of the cars were torched.
That's not vandalism.
Shops in the Janpath were looted.
That's not vandalism.
What is vandalism then?
What is vandalism?
If the same thing would have been repeated today at the Prime Minister's house, who would have been responsible?
I mean, in the name of protest, in the name of democracy, this is nothing but anarchy.
And that too by a party who has ruled this country for 60 long years.
What would have happened if after post-Delhi riots, all the Sikhs would have gathered at the Prime Minister's house
What would have happened when Babri Masjid was really opened and all the Hindus would have gathered outside the Prime Minister's house?
What would have happened?
Is this the kind of protest, this utter frustration, nothing else?
You are not in power because of democracy.
You have to learn and respect democracy.
It's no cackling anymore.
It's no... Dr. Shama Mohamad wants to respond to you.
Dr. Shama Mohamad wants to respond to you.
The BJP alleges that this is planned conspiracy by the Congress party.
It is, it is anarchy.
These are planned instances just to coincide with the parliament session, ma'am.
I want to know, Gaurav, what is not a planned thing.
Any time there is a protest, it is called a planned protest.
When our farmers protested in this country, more than 700 of them died.
They were left at the Delhi border.
They were not allowed to enter.
What did they call them?
Khalistani, urban naxal.
So, anybody protests in this country, they have a name.
I have never heard of this before 2014.
Like Aarti Ji said, there have been innumerable protests by senior leaders.
I remember Arun Jaitley and Sushma Swaraj Ji protesting on the streets with gas cylinders, various protests during our time.
Did we stop them?
Because we believe in a democracy, it is their right to protest.
We did not take them and we did not say, oh, they are at the prime minister's house.
They are going to kill the prime minister.
Just like this police officer was saying, he's saying it's gundagarti.
I mean, there is a peaceful protest.
And Ajay Alok used the word vandalism and anarchy.
I don't see any vandalism and anarchy where Rahul Gandhi is protesting.
We do not have guns.
We do not have knives.
It is a peaceful protest because the prime minister refuses to take action.
There is no accountability in this country.
The speaker of this country is with the Prime Minister and the party because you have a TMC which is broken and then you tell part of the members to join a party called Citizens Party of India.
Now tomorrow you would have a party, DMK for example or a TDP, people break up from there, they join a new party which is made
I mean, have you heard of something like this before 2014?
And then they are told to sit in another place.
The election commission is in the hand of the prime minister.
The ED goes knocking on the doors of who the prime minister of India want.
Now, if the system is broken, if the system is broken, what do you do?
You come out on the street.
The police officers said about gundagardhi, I want to know when CM Yogi Adityanath threatens openly Muslims, threatens openly, is that not gundagardhi?
Demolishing a college, demolishing a university, you can take over the university from the person, but demolishing 38 of its buildings, I've never heard of it, isn't that gundagardhi?
No, but is that happening as per law and if it's illegal then you must protest in a court of law.

You know, while that's a separate debate, while that's a separate debate, while that's a separate debate, the MH Johar University, that's what you're referring to, can land be illegally acquired even to build a university?
There are illegal number of buildings, innumerable number of illegal buildings in our country, and I can give you a list of it.
Alright?
Now when it is, if that particular person has made a mall, a hotel, please go and demolish it because he was earning money through, you know, this.
But this is when you're educating a system.
Education is something which we all require, which anybody requires.
So I believe that.
And the other thing... Even if it's an illegally acquired land.
Fair enough.
R.T.
Jarrett, you want to respond?
I just want to say that I think we're straying from the topic.
Dr. Sharma Mohamad, Aarti Jairat wants to respond to you and Dr. Vikram Singh, but go on.
I'm saying that I think we're straying from the topic.
And I don't think we need to go into what Yogi Adityanath is doing in UP.
We're talking about what's happening in Delhi right now.
And I would like to remind Ajay Alok.
And I'm surprised that he's talking.
He comes from a party which we have seen on the streets for years and years leading demonstrations against price rise, against gasoline hike, against
all kinds of things we've seen them for years and years and years and you know now you're saying that this is anarchy
I mean, your party was absolutely, I remember in the 90s, early 90s, your party was out on the streets all the time, from Motherland Khurana to LK Advani.
And when those whole anti-Mandal demonstrations were happening, there were many BJP leaders who were out there also.
And you're now talking about anarchy.
So I think that we're really losing sight of what democracy means.
We're so caught up with this whole thing of law and order and security that we are now building so many barricades between the people and the government.
And I think that is what was the spirit of the protest when your anchor, your channel, Deegharam,
was talking to these kids who were out on the streets, and they were saying, we want accountability.
What did they mean by accountability?
They mean close that gap between us and the government, which seems to be increasing day by day because everything gets reduced to security.
OK.
Dr. Ajay Alok wants to respond before I bring Dr. Vikram Singh to keep this.
Democracy needs accountability, Gaurav.
There is no accountability in this country.
OK.
Dr. Ajay Alok wants to respond.
If you want to see democracy from the leftists,
vision and from the spectacle of a leftist or a spectacle of someone who doesn't believe in democracy.
Yes, that could be a definition of your democracy.
Ma'am, if you remember, we were on the streets all the time, not even from Madanlal, Khurrana days, even from Vajpayee days, Madhwani days.
Give me one instance of my party where we have not taken up permission and we have done nothing lawful.
where our rallies have gone into vandalism, where we have broken the cars, where we have looted the houses, what happened yesterday.
You are mum on that.
You are selectively choosing today.
I don't think Rahul Gandhi was... I am not trying to defend Rahul Gandhi, but was Rahul Gandhi vandalizing a car today?
Was Rahul Gandhi vandalizing a car?
One by one.
Dr. Ajay Alok, then Dr. Vikram Singh first.
Go on.
For that matter, any sensible person.
You are talking about accountability.
8 to 10 years old coming in a rally and indulging in stone pelting.
Do you think it's accountable for their parents to make that happen?
I mean, any kind of logic.
What does a 10-year-old, a 12-year-old, an 8-year-old kid have to do with a rally?
Why he or she was there at any point of time?
And Delhi police have given a clarification that they have not done anything.
Well, why Rao Gandhi, all the way, he'll go to the Prime Minister's house?
That's the only place left for demonstration.
Okay, can I say something?
But it's the job of the opposition to make headlines, sir.
It's the job of the opposition, Dr. Ajay Alok, to make headlines.
And if Rahul Gandhi is making headlines by being at 7 LKM, you know, he's achieved his aim.
But I want to bring in Dr. Vikram Singh into this conversation.
Dr. Vikram Singh, you had raised your hand when Dr. Shama Mohammed was talking about anarchy.
or responding to allegations of anarchy in Uttar Pradesh.
You want to respond, sir?
Yes, Gauravji.
Three quick points to learn at Dr. Shama Mohammed's points.
Number one, that the Prime Minister's house is sacrosanct and a sanitized area.
Nobody can take liberties there.
Point number one.
It is by no stretch of imagination.
Is it a peaceful agitation?
Whatever be the reason, there is a way of doing it.
Put an application, get the permission from the police.
You don't want permission.
Then it is an illegal.
Then Shama Ji, it is an illegal agitation.
We will hit the street without permission.
It is illegal.
Everything is under them.
They control everything.
We will not permission.
Be prepared for the consequences.
Then be prepared for the consequences.
We are prepared for the consequences.
We are ready for this country.
Wonderful.
Wonderful.
Wonderful.
Wonderful.

The Delhi Police Commissioner and the Delhi Police to investigate and take the hardest possible action as per law against those who are violating the law of this land, at the same time, accountability.
I will let that be the key word today.
I want to thank Aarti Jherat, Dr. Shama Mohammed, Dr. Ajay Alok and Dr. Vikram Singh for joining me on this India First special broadcast.
We need accountability.
We want our exam systems to be absolutely pure.
and untarnished by that cottage industry called Paperleak Mafia.
We'll be tracking that story very closely.
